notes: Fixture for scripts/eval-kb-rerank.ts. Synthetic, PHI-free: every passage is
facility policy or Florida ALF regulation, no resident data.
Candidates are listed in simulated RRF order — the order a retriever would
hand the reranker — so position 0 is what you get with no rerank at all.
The correct passage is deliberately never first.
Distractors are on-topic and wrong, not off-topic: each mentions the subject
without supplying the specific provision asked for. A set of clean archetypes
cannot tell a good reranker from a bad one.
One label was corrected after the first run. The staffing query originally read
'minimum staffing at night', which the awake-overnight rule answers better than
the weekly-hours rule it was labelled against — the reranker was right and the
fixture was wrong. The query was reworded so the label is unambiguous. No
threshold or prompt was changed to fit the result.

cases.query: How quickly does a medication error have to be reported?

candidates.excerpt: All medication errors must be reported. Staff are reminded that a culture of safety depends on errors being disclosed rather than concealed, and no disciplinary action follows from good-faith reporting.
Medication errors are recorded on the Medication Error Report form, which is retained in the facility's quality assurance file and reviewed at the quarterly QA meeting.

The nurse or med-tech discovering a medication error shall notify the administrator and the resident's health care provider within 24 hours of discovery, and shall document the notification in the resident's record at the time it is made.
Unlicensed staff assisting with self-administration complete four hours of initial medication training and two hours annually thereafter, delivered by Baya or an equivalent approved provider.
Section 4: Medication Errors. 4.1 Definitions. 4.2 Discovery and Notification. 4.3 Documentation. 4.4 Quality Assurance Review.
Adverse incidents as defined in section 429.23 are reported to the Agency within 1 business day of the incident, with the full report following within 15 days.

cases.query: Who is allowed to sign the Form 1823?

candidates.excerpt: The AHCA Form 1823 Resident Health Assessment is the legal entry point for admission and must be on file before a resident takes occupancy.
A Form 1823 completed more than 90 days before admission is not acceptable and must be repeated before the resident moves in.

The health assessment must be completed and signed by a licensed physician, a physician assistant, or an advanced practice registered nurse licensed under chapter 464. A registered nurse may not sign in their place.
Completed 1823s are filed in the resident's clinical record and retained for five years following discharge.
Appendix B: Forms referenced in this procedure — Form 1823, Form 1823A, DCF Form 2506, SSA-787.
A copy of the signed assessment is provided to the resident or the resident's representative on request at no charge.

cases.query: How many staff hours per week does a 52 bed facility have to provide?

candidates.excerpt: A facility with 17 or more residents shall have at least one staff member awake at all hours of the night.
The administrator shall be available to the facility 24 hours a day and shall designate in writing a staff member to act in their absence.
Facilities with 51 to 75 residents shall provide a minimum of 297 staff hours per week. These are direct care hours and do not include the administrator, food service, or housekeeping personnel.
All direct care staff complete the core training curriculum within 30 days of employment and are certified by the facility administrator.
Circle of Life staffs above the statutory minimum wherever census and acuity allow; the minimum is a floor, not a target.
(1) Staffing standards. (2) Minimum staffing hours. (3) Awake staff. (4) Administrator availability. (5) Staff records.

cases.query: Do we have to notify anyone when a resident elopes and comes back unharmed?

candidates.excerpt: Residents assessed at risk of elopement are identified on admission and reassessed quarterly, and the risk is noted in the service plan.
The facility conducts an elopement drill at least annually and documents staff participation.
On discovering a resident is missing, staff initiate an immediate search of the building and grounds and notify the administrator.

Elopement is a reportable adverse incident whether or not the resident was injured and whether or not the resident returned voluntarily. The 1-business-day report to the Agency is required in every case.
The resident's representative is contacted as soon as practicable after a resident is found.
An incident resulting in death, brain damage, spinal damage, or a fracture requires notification within 1 business day.

cases.query: How long do we keep an employee's file after they leave?

candidates.excerpt: Each employee file contains the application, level 2 background screening results, job description, training records, and annual evaluations.
Resident clinical records are retained for five years following discharge or death.
Employees may review their own personnel file on request, in the presence of the administrator or designee.
Personnel records are retained for two years following separation of employment, after which they are destroyed by shredding and the destruction logged.
Background screening is repeated every five years for all staff with direct resident contact.
Contents: resident records, personnel records, financial records, incident files, quality assurance files.

cases.query: Can an ALF resident keep and take their own medication?

candidates.excerpt: Centrally stored medications are kept in a locked cabinet accessible only to staff authorized to assist with self-administration.
Assistance with self-administration includes reading the label aloud, opening the container, and steadying the resident's hand, but does not include placing the medication in the resident's mouth.

A resident who is capable of self-administration may keep their own medication in their own room, provided it is stored so that other residents cannot access it. No physician order is required for a resident to self-administer.
Medications administered by a licensed nurse require a current order from the resident's health care provider.
A medication observation record is maintained for each resident receiving assistance with self-administration.
(1) Definitions. (2) Self-administration. (3) Assistance with self-administration. (4) Administration. (5) Storage and disposal.

cases.query: What temperature does the walk-in cooler need to be kept at?

candidates.excerpt: At least one person responsible for food service holds a current food handler certification.
Menus are planned by a registered dietitian and posted where residents can read them, one week in advance.
Refrigeration temperatures are logged twice daily by dietary staff and the log is reviewed weekly by the dietary manager.

Refrigerated storage is maintained at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. Freezer storage is maintained at 0 degrees Fahrenheit or below. A unit found out of range is emptied and the contents assessed for discard.
Hot foods are held at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above until served.
Section 6: Storage. 6.1 Dry storage. 6.2 Refrigerated storage. 6.3 Freezer storage. 6.4 Temperature logs.

cases.query: How much notice before we can discharge someone for nonpayment?

candidates.excerpt: A resident may be discharged when the facility can no longer meet the resident's needs, for nonpayment, or when the resident's continued residence poses a danger to themselves or others.

The facility provides the resident and the resident's representative 45 days written notice of discharge. The notice states the reason and the resident's right to contest it through the long-term care ombudsman.
Where a resident poses an immediate danger, discharge may occur on shorter notice, with the reason documented and the ombudsman notified the same day.
Prepaid amounts covering the period after discharge are refunded within 45 days of the resident vacating the unit.
The administrator assists the resident in locating an appropriate alternative placement before the discharge date.
Accounts 30 days past due receive a written reminder; accounts 60 days past due are referred to the administrator.
